Quotient stacks<FOOTNOTEOPEN_0001>In the literature,
<EMPHOPEN_0001>quotient stack<EMPHCLOSE_0001> often means a stack of the
form <MATH_0001> with <MATH_0002> an algebraic space and <MATH_0003> a subgroup scheme
of <MATH_0004> rather than an arbitrary flat group scheme.<FOOTNOTECLOSE_0001>
form a very important subclass of Artin stacks which include almost all moduli
stacks studied by algebraic geometers. The geometry of a quotient stack
<MATH_0005> is the <MATH_0006>-equivariant geometry of <MATH_0007>. It is often easier to show
properties are true for quotient stacks and some results are only known to be
true for quotient stacks. The following papers address: When is an algebraic
stack a global quotient stack? Is an algebraic stack ``locally'' a quotient
stack?

<REF_0003>
<STRUCT_0010>
A stack has the resolution property if every coherent sheaf is the quotient of
a vector bundle. The first main theorem is that if <MATH_0033> is a normal

the following are equivalent: (1) <MATH_0034> has the resolution property and
(2)

stacks have the resolution property was proven by Thomason.
The second main theorem is that if <MATH_0041> is a smooth Deligne-Mumford
stack over
a field which has a finite and generically trivial stabilizer group

<STRUCT_0012> Kresch: <EMPHOPEN_0004>On the Geometry of Deligne-Mumford Stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0004>
<REF_0004>
<STRUCT_0013>
This article summarizes general structure results of Deligne-Mumford
stacks (of finite type over a field) and contains some interesting results
concerning quotient stacks. It is shown that any smooth, separated,
generically tame Deligne-Mumford stack with quasi-projective coarse moduli
space is a quotient stack <MATH_0046> with <MATH_0047> quasi-projective and <MATH_0048> an
algebraic group. If <MATH_0049> is a Deligne-Mumford stack whose coarse
moduli space
is a scheme, then <MATH_0050> is Zariski-locally a quotient stack if and only
if it
admits a Zariski-open covering by stack quotients of schemes by finite groups.
If <MATH_0051> is a Deligne-Mumford stack proper over a field of
characteristic 0
with coarse moduli space <MATH_0052>, then: <MATH_0053> is projective and <MATH_0054> is a
quotient stack if and only if <MATH_0055> is projective and <MATH_0056>
possesses a generating sheaf if and only if
<MATH_0057> admits a closed embedding into a smooth proper DM stack with
projective
coarse moduli space. This motivates a definition that a Deligne-Mumford stack
is <EMPHOPEN_0005>projective<EMPHCLOSE_0005> if there exists a closed embedding into a smooth, proper
Deligne-Mumford stack with projective coarse moduli space.

<STRUCT_0018> Kresch: <EMPHOPEN_0007>Cycle Groups for Artin Stacks<EMPHCLOSE_0007> <REF_0006>
<STRUCT_0019>
It is shown that a reduced Artin stack finite type over a field with affine
stabilizer groups admits a stratification by quotient stacks.
